root_cause.text: The `xchk_quota_item` function acquires `dq->q_qlock` but fails to release it before returning early when `xchk_fblock_process_error` returns false, causing a lock leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that `dq->q_qlock` is held throughout the function execution, but the early return path at line 174 (after `xchk_fblock_process_error` returns false) did not include a `mutex_unlock(&dq->q_qlock)` call. The fix adds `mutex_unlock(&dq->q_qlock)` immediately before the early return statement, ensuring the lock is released in all code paths. This is a classic lock acquisition/release asymmetry bug where one exit path was missing the corresponding unlock operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mutex lock leak by unlocking dq->q_qlock before returning from error path in xchk_quota_item().
intent_record.what: Added mutex_unlock(&dq->q_qlock) call before the early return statement in the error handling path of xchk_quota_item(). The unlock is placed inside braces that were added around the existing return statement.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the quota lock (q_qlock) is properly released when an error occurs during quota item block map checking. Previously, if xchk_fblock_process_error() returned false (indicating error processing failed), the function would return without unlocking the mutex, causing a lock leak. Now the mutex is explicitly unlocked before returning.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
xfs: check the ondisk space mapping behind a dquot

Each xfs_dquot object caches the file offset and daddr of the ondisk
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 7d1f0e167a067ed741dec08b7614d76893422b04
Author: Darrick J. Wong <djwong@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Dec 15 10:03:44 2023 -0800

    xfs: check the ondisk space mapping behind a dquot
    
    Each xfs_dquot object caches the file offset and daddr of the ondisk
    block that backs the dquot.  Make sure these cached values are the same
    as the bmapi data, and that the block state is written.
    
    Signed-off-by: Darrick J. Wong <djwong@kernel.org>
    Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is present in this commit. At lines 159-161, the code calls `xchk_iunlock(sc, XFS_ILOCK_SHARED)` to release the inode lock, then calls `xchk_fblock_process_error(sc, XFS_DATA_FORK, offset, &error)`. If this function returns false (indicating an error should be returned), the code executes `return error` at line 161. However, the dquot lock (`dq->q_qlock`) acquired at line 147 (`xfs_dqlock(dq)`) is never released before this early return. The lock was acquired after unlocking and re-locking the dquot (lines 145-147), but there is no corresponding `xfs_dqunlock(dq)` call before the early return on line 161, causing a lock leak when `xchk_fblock_process_error` returns false.
